questions.text: Reliance on Digital ID (KYC): Economy-wide impact: (1) Integration with Banks (e-KYC); (2) Integration with Telcos (SIM Reg); (3) Integration with Fintechs; (4) Cost of verification API (affordable?); (5) Reliability impact on business (downtime cost); (6) Liability for ID errors; (7) Data sharing protocols.
questions.evidence_required: API usage stats, SLA agreements, Business impact assessments
questions.africa_specific_notes: The private sector is the biggest user of Digital ID. If the API is expensive or unreliable, the digital economy stalls.

questions.text: GovTech Vendor Ecosystem: Local capacity: (1) Share of contracts to local firms; (2) Technology transfer programs; (3) Open standards adoption (to avoid lock-in); (4) Innovation challenges/Hackathons; (5) Startup procurement policy; (6) Intellectual Property rights; (7) Sustainability of local vendors.
questions.evidence_required: Procurement data (local vs foreign), Innovation program reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Governments often buy from foreign giants (Idemia, Thales) ignoring local tech ecosystem. Building local capacity ensures long-term sustainability.

questions.text: Civil Society Oversight & Engagement: The watchdog role: (1) Freedom of operation for NGOs; (2) Consultation in policy making; (3) Access to information; (4) Strategic litigation (court cases); (5) Public awareness campaigns; (6) Protection of activists; (7) Funding independence.
questions.evidence_required: Consultation minutes, Court case records, NGO reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Civil society (e.g., Nubian Rights Forum in Kenya) has been the main check on ID abuse. They need space to operate.

questions.text: Donor Dependency & Conditionality: Who drives the agenda?: (1) Percentage of budget funded by donors; (2) Alignment with national priorities (vs donor interests); (3) Sustainability after donor exit; (4) Technology choices influenced by donors; (5) Transparency of donor agreements; (6) Capacity building component; (7) Sovereignty impact.
questions.evidence_required: Project financing docs, Donor agreements, Sustainability plan
questions.africa_specific_notes: World Bank 'ID4D' is a major driver. Risks include 'copy-paste' solutions and lack of local ownership.

questions.text: Cross-Border Identity & Travel: Regional mobility: (1) Recognition of ID as travel document (e.g., EAC ID); (2) Interoperability with neighbors; (3) One Network Area (roaming/calls); (4) Mutual recognition of professional certs; (5) Data sharing for security; (6) Border control efficiency; (7) Refugee management.
questions.evidence_required: Regional protocols, Border crossing stats, Interoperability specs
questions.africa_specific_notes: EAC (East African Community) allows travel with ID. AfCFTA (Free Trade Area) requires trusted identity for trade.

questions.text: Harmonization of Standards: Speaking the same language: (1) Adherence to international standards (ICAO, ISO); (2) Regional data protection harmonization; (3) Cybersecurity cooperation; (4) Payment system linkage (PAPSS); (5) Digital signature recognition; (6) Regulatory convergence; (7) Knowledge sharing.
questions.africa_specific_notes: Fragmented standards hinder trade. Harmonization is key for the African Single Digital Market.

questions.text: Public Trust in Government Digital Systems: The ultimate metric: (1) Citizen satisfaction surveys; (2) Adoption rates of e-services; (3) Trust in data privacy; (4) Perception of corruption; (5) Willingness to register; (6) Feedback loop effectiveness; (7) Media sentiment.
questions.evidence_required: Survey results, Adoption curves, Media analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: Trust is low. History of misuse (e.g., using census for tax/conscription) makes people wary. Building trust takes years.

questions.text: Digital Divide & Social Equity: Impact on society: (1) Gap between rural/urban adoption; (2) Gender gap in ID ownership; (3) Impact on poverty reduction (social safety nets); (4) Cost of access (device/data); (5) Digital literacy barrier; (6) Role of intermediaries; (7) Equity impact assessment.
questions.evidence_required: Equity audits, Household surveys, Impact evaluations
questions.africa_specific_notes: Digitization can widen the gap. If the poor can't get an ID, they disappear from the state's view.

scoring_notes: Layer 6 (Ecosystem) for Government in SSA: The private sector needs the ID system to work. Civil society needs it to be fair. Donors need it to be sustainable. The public needs to trust it.
